Introduction and results

A princess moves through a building every night. Each morning a searcher may open several doors. The princess knows the search plan, may start anywhere, and must move to an adjacent room after each unsuccessful day. The problem is to guarantee capture as quickly as possible. Even on a single corridor the answer has a parity correction: dividing the amount of uncertainty by the apparent daily progress is not always enough.

This is a minimum-time version of the Hunters and Rabbit game. A path PnP_nPn​ has nnn vertices, and Pn1□⋯□PndP_{n_1}\mathbin{\square}\cdots\mathbin{\square}P_{n_d}Pn1​​□⋯□Pnd​​ denotes the Cartesian box with those side lengths. Write Tm(G)T_m(G)Tm​(G) for the optimal guaranteed number of inspection days, with value ∞\infty∞ when no finite guarantee exists. Section 2 specifies the order of inspection and compulsory movement precisely.

The structural results

The common difficulty is temporal. A small possible-position set may have a particularly favorable next neighborhood, but that neighborhood need not contain an equally favorable set for the following day. We retain a history bit where necessary, and also prove a more general comparison theorem. A monotone, cardinality-preserving set map CCC with N(C(A))⊆C(N(A))N(C(A))\subseteq C(N(A))N(C(A))⊆C(N(A)) compresses a whole strategy without increasing any day’s inspection budget. Idempotent maps supply an exact optimal-strategy normal form. This assertion is stronger than a one-step isoperimetric inequality.

We construct such operators from odd paths and square diagonal shifts. They give exact recurrences on smaller families of states in arbitrary dimension. More strongly, on every box whose side lengths are all odd, we prove that the restricted simplicial orders minimize open neighborhoods and that neighborhoods of prefixes are prefixes. An induction using fiber compressions and a weighted exchange lemma reduces the unrestricted game to two cardinalities. The resulting exact algorithm is polynomial in the number of rooms and returns an optimal schedule. A recurrence remains distinct from a closed expression: the general box problem is not declared solved by the existence of an exponential search over all possible-position sets.

The three-dimensional example has a particularly concise answer: m0 ⁣: ⁣4567 ⁣: ⁣89 ⁣: ⁣111213 ⁣: ⁣2627 or moreTm(P33)∞181064321.\begin{array}{c|rrrrrrrr} m&0\!:\!4&5&6&7\!:\!8&9\!:\!11&12&13\!:\!26&27\text{ or more}\\\hline T_m(P_3^3)&\infty&18&10&6&4&3&2&1. \end{array}mTm​(P33​)​0:4∞​518​610​7:86​9:114​123​13:262​27 or more1.​​ Its complete lower and upper proofs are checked in Lean. A separate height construction proves h(P3□P3□Pn)=5h(P_3\mathbin{\square}P_3\mathbin{\square}P_n)=5h(P3​□P3​□Pn​)=5 for n≥3n\ge3n≥3, where h(G)h(G)h(G) is the minimum feasible daily budget.

Prior work and provenance

Britnell and Wildon (Britnell and Wildon 2013) studied the princess puzzle with one daily inspection, including the path value 2n−42n-42n−4. Haslegrave studied the associated evasion game (Haslegrave 2014); related moving- target search appears in Beluhov and Kolev (Beluhov and Kolev 2017). Abramovskaya, Fomin, Golovach, and Pilipczuk (Abramovskaya et al. 2016) developed Hunters and Rabbit results, including the rectangular-grid feasibility threshold ⌊min⁡(a,b)/2⌋+1\left\lfloor\min(a,b)/2\right\rfloor+1⌊min(a,b)/2⌋+1. Bolkema and Groothuis proved isoperimetric nesting and the hunting number for hypercubes (Bolkema and Groothuis 2019). We use precise versions of these results; minimum-time claims do not follow from feasibility alone. Parity-restricted boundary minimization on the binary cube goes back to Körner and Wei (Körner and Wei 1984). Compression proofs and local-to-global principles have a substantial earlier literature, including Bezrukov and Serra (Bezrukov and Serra 2002); their closed-neighborhood theorem is distinct from the open-neighborhood argument given here.

Dmitry Kamenetsky recorded conjectural two- and three-inspection path formulas in March 2018 (Kamenetsky 2018a, 2018b). Equation (1) proves those special cases and extends them to arbitrary budgets. The author’s independent path work took place between October 2019 and March 2020 and was written in two Bulgarian conference manuscripts (Raychev and Rusev 2020; Raychev 2020). The one-probe restriction omitted from a printed general formula is made explicit here. The original conference documents are preserved.

The time-budget inverse parameter is also considered in recent work (Ben-Ameur et al. 2026); we do not claim the general optimization question as new. Recontamination can matter substantially on general graphs (Dissaux et al. 2025), so a presumed monotone search is never used as an unproved lower-bound assumption. Classical closed-neighborhood isoperimetry for Cartesian grids (Otachi and Suda 2011) supplies one of our higher-dimensional applications. Our use of that theorem is distinguished from the open-neighborhood argument for odd rectangles.

Remark 1.1 (Status of this manuscript). This is a research manuscript in preparation, not an arXiv submission. The ordinary theorems have internal independent proof reviews; exact Lean coverage is stated in Section 14. Attribution of the 2026 extensions is still undergoing a focused literature review. The manuscript makes no blanket claim that every derived ingredient is new to the literature.

The game and its possible positions

Let G=(V,E)G=(V,E)G=(V,E) be a finite simple graph without isolated vertices, and let m≥1m\geq1m≥1 be the daily inspection budget. Every connected board with at least two rooms satisfies this graph assumption; a one-room board takes one inspection and is treated separately. The target chooses an unknown initial vertex. On day t=1,2,…t=1,2,\ldotst=1,2,…, the searcher inspects a set St⊆VS_t\subseteq VSt​⊆V with ∣St∣≤m|S_t|\leq m∣St​∣≤m. If the target occupies a vertex of StS_tSt​, it is caught. Otherwise it must move along exactly one edge before the next day. Inspections within a day are simultaneous. The searcher receives no information about an unsuccessful inspection other than the miss.

Write Tm(G)T_m(G)Tm​(G) for the minimum number of days in which capture can be guaranteed, and put Tm(G)=∞T_m(G)=\inftyTm​(G)=∞ if there is no finite guarantee. The associated feasibility threshold is h(G)=min⁡{m≥1:Tm(G)<∞}.h(G)=\min\{m\geq1:T_m(G)<\infty\}.h(G)=min{m≥1:Tm​(G)<∞}. We consider deterministic guarantees. Before capture, every observation is a miss. Thus an adaptive strategy has only one continuing observation history and is represented by a sequence (St)t≥1(S_t)_{t\geq1}(St​)t≥1​. This sequence formulation does not restrict the searcher’s guaranteed performance.

For A⊆VA\subseteq VA⊆V, its open neighborhood is N(A)={v∈V:some u∈A satisfies uv∈E}.N(A)=\{v\in V:\text{some }u\in A\text{ satisfies }uv\in E\}.N(A)={v∈V:some u∈A satisfies uv∈E}. Define the possible-position sets immediately before inspection by B1=V,Bt+1=N(Bt∖St).B_1=V,\qquad B_{t+1}=N(B_t\setminus S_t).B1​=V,Bt+1​=N(Bt​∖St​). The following elementary interpretation is used in every subsequent argument.

Lemma 2.1. For each t≥1t\geq1t≥1, a vertex vvv belongs to BtB_tBt​ if and only if there is a walk v1,…,vt=vv_1,\ldots,v_t=vv1​,…,vt​=v in GGG such that vi∉Siv_i\notin S_ivi​∈/Si​ for every 1≤i<t1\leq i<t1≤i<t. Consequently capture is guaranteed by day ttt exactly when Bt⊆StB_t\subseteq S_tBt​⊆St​.

Proof. The assertion about walks follows by induction. At t=1t=1t=1 every vertex is an admissible initial position. For the inductive step, v∈Bt+1v\in B_{t+1}v∈Bt+1​ means that some neighbor u∈Btu\in B_tu∈Bt​ avoids StS_tSt​. Append vvv to a walk ending at uuu supplied by the induction hypothesis. Conversely, the penultimate vertex of any such walk belongs to Bt∖StB_t\setminus S_tBt​∖St​, so its final vertex belongs to Bt+1B_{t+1}Bt+1​.

A walk ending outside StS_tSt​ avoids all inspections through day ttt, whereas every surviving walk is caught that day if its endpoint lies in StS_tSt​. This is exactly the stated inclusion. ◻

Since GGG has no isolated vertices, a nonempty set has a nonempty open neighborhood. Hence the capture condition is also equivalent to Bt+1=∅B_{t+1}=\varnothingBt+1​=∅. We use this equivalent form only under that hypothesis. A board with a single room is handled directly: one inspection on the first day suffices. Thus an inability to make a move is never silently treated as capture.

Two monotonicity observations will be useful. Starting from fewer possible positions cannot make a fixed inspection sequence less successful, and adding inspected vertices cannot make it less successful. Both follow by induction from monotonicity of NNN and set difference in their respective arguments. In particular, probes outside the current possible-position set may be wasted, but they cause no problem for the model or the lower bounds.

Two initial parity classes

Suppose GGG is bipartite, with vertex classes V0,V1V_0,V_1V0​,V1​. Keep track of the two possible initial colors separately: R1s=Vs,Rt+1s=N(Rts∖St),s∈{0,1}.R^s_1=V_s,\qquad R^s_{t+1}=N(R^s_t\setminus S_t),\qquad s\in\{0,1\}.R1s​=Vs​,Rt+1s​=N(Rts​∖St​),s∈{0,1}. Then Bt=Rt0∪˙Rt1,Rts⊆Vs+t−1(mod2).B_t=R^0_t\mathbin{\dot\cup}R^1_t, \qquad R^s_t\subseteq V_{s+t-1\pmod2}.Bt​=Rt0​∪˙Rt1​,Rts​⊆Vs+t−1(mod2)​. Indeed, neighborhood and deletion distribute over unions, and every edge reverses color. The two sets therefore stay disjoint while exchanging their current colors each night. Allocations to the two initial classes sum to at most the day’s inspection budget. We will state explicitly whether a pair of counts is indexed by initial color or by current color; the latter convention swaps the two counts after every move.

This separates the bookkeeping common to the path, ladder, and grid arguments. The work specific to a graph is to determine how small a neighborhood can be after a given number of inspections, and when a sequence of such bounds can actually be attained.

Compressing entire strategies

An isoperimetric inequality bounds one neighborhood. To preserve an optimal search, the replacement sets must also respect containment and remain compatible after successive moves. The following criterion provides that stronger conclusion.

A strategy compression on GGG is a map C:2V→2VC:2^V\to2^VC:2V→2V satisfying A⊆B  ⟹  C(A)⊆C(B),∣C(A)∣=∣A∣,N(C(A))⊆C(N(A)).\begin{aligned} A\subseteq B&\implies C(A)\subseteq C(B), \\ |C(A)|&=|A|, \\ N(C(A))&\subseteq C(N(A)). \end{aligned}A⊆B∣C(A)∣N(C(A))​⟹C(A)⊆C(B),=∣A∣,⊆C(N(A)).​(6, 7, 8) Idempotence is an additional property, not part of this definition.

Products and simultaneous compression

Lemma 3.3 (Product lift). A strategy compression on a graph AAA lifts to A□HA\mathbin{\square}HA□H by applying it separately in every HHH-indexed AAA-fiber. Idempotence is preserved.

Proof. Write ShS_hSh​ for the fiber at hhh. Its neighborhood is N(S)h=NA(Sh)∪⋃u∼hSu.N(S)_h=N_A(S_h)\cup\bigcup_{u\sim h}S_u.N(S)h​=NA​(Sh​)∪u∼h⋃​Su​. For the lifted operator C^\widehat CC, the corresponding neighborhood is N(C^(S))h=NA(C(Sh))∪⋃u∼hC(Su)⊆C(NA(Sh))∪⋃u∼hC(Su)⊆C(NA(Sh)∪⋃u∼hSu).\begin{aligned} N(\widehat C(S))_h &=N_A(C(S_h))\cup\bigcup_{u\sim h}C(S_u)\\ &\subseteq C(N_A(S_h))\cup\bigcup_{u\sim h}C(S_u)\\ &\subseteq C\left(N_A(S_h)\cup\bigcup_{u\sim h}S_u\right). \end{aligned}N(C(S))h​​=NA​(C(Sh​))∪u∼h⋃​C(Su​)⊆C(NA​(Sh​))∪u∼h⋃​C(Su​)⊆C(NA​(Sh​)∪u∼h⋃​Su​).​ The last inclusion uses monotonicity separately on each input subset of the union. Cardinality, monotonicity and idempotence hold fiber by fiber. ◻

Compositions of strategy compressions are strategy compressions, since N(C(D(S)))⊆C(N(D(S)))⊆C(D(N(S))).N(C(D(S)))\subseteq C(N(D(S)))\subseteq C(D(N(S))).N(C(D(S)))⊆C(N(D(S)))⊆C(D(N(S))). Suppose finitely many such operators strictly decrease a common nonnegative integer potential whenever they change a set. If that potential has a uniform upper bound BBB, cycling through all operators B+1B+1B+1 times reaches a common fixed point for every input. A cycle with a change decreases the potential, and a cycle without a change fixes every operator. The resulting map is a composition with a uniform number of factors, hence is monotone and cardinality preserving; it is also idempotent. This avoids assuming that an input-dependent stopping rule preserves monotonicity.

Square fibers and equal-sided boxes

Abramovskaya, Fomin, Golovach and Pilipczuk (Abramovskaya et al. 2016, sec. 3.1, Lemma 2) prove that diagonal shifts do not increase the neighborhood size of a one-color set in a square. The following fiber calculation strengthens the scalar comparison to (8) and applies it to both colors. That stronger statement is what allows whole strategies to be compressed.

Lemma 3.5 (Square diagonal compression). On {0,…,n−1}2\{0,\ldots,n-1\}^2{0,…,n−1}2, compress each line x+y=kx+y=kx+y=k toward increasing priority for smaller yyy, keeping its selected cardinality. This is an idempotent, parity-preserving strategy compression. The same is true on lines x−y=kx-y=kx−y=k, again toward smaller yyy.

Proof. Only the neighborhood inclusion needs proof. Consecutive square diagonals have lengths differing by one. Index both from the common increasing-yyy end. From a diagonal of length LLL to one of length L+1L+1L+1, a selected index jjj has neighbors j,j+1j,j+1j,j+1. A nonempty aaa-set therefore has at least a+1a+1a+1 neighbors; a prefix attains this bound with a prefix. From length LLL to length L−1L-1L−1, the indices are j−1,jj-1,jj−1,j, clipped to the valid range. A proper nonempty aaa-set has at least aaa neighbors, and the full set has L−1L-1L−1. Indeed, if it has ccc consecutive blocks and occupies eee endpoints, its neighbor count is a+c−ea+c-ea+c−e; for a proper set c≥ec\geq ec≥e. Prefixes again attain the bounds with prefixes.

Fix an output diagonal. Its two input diagonals, after compression, contribute prefixes from the same end. Their union is the longer prefix. Each contributing length is no larger than its original contribution, hence no larger than the original union’s size. The compressed union is therefore contained in the prefix selected by compressing that original neighborhood. This argument works on either parity and on their union. Reflecting xxx proves the other diagonal direction. ◻

Theorem 3.6 (Normal form on equal-sided boxes). The same operators are available within every group of equal-length coordinates in an arbitrary Cartesian box. Odd-coordinate path compressions can be included simultaneously.

Proof. Lift both square operators to every pair i<ji<ji<j of equal coordinates. They compress toward smaller xjx_jxj​ on lines xi+xj=kx_i+x_j=kxi​+xj​=k and xi−xj=kx_i-x_j=kxi​−xj​=k. Use the potential E(S)=∑v∈S∑i=1divi.\mathcal E(S)=\sum_{v\in S}\sum_{i=1}^d i v_i.E(S)=v∈S∑​i=1∑d​ivi​. A nontrivial plus-diagonal transfer by δ>0\delta>0δ>0 decreases it by (j−i)δ(j-i)\delta(j−i)δ, and a minus-diagonal transfer by (i+j)δ(i+j)\delta(i+j)δ. An odd-coordinate prefix transfer also strictly decreases it. The potential is uniformly bounded; on PndP_n^dPnd​ the bound nd(n−1)d(d+1)/2n^d(n-1)d(d+1)/2nd(n−1)d(d+1)/2 suffices. Uniform cycling therefore gives an idempotent strategy compression. Its fixed sets are precisely the ideals for the displayed local moves, with the additional −2ei-2e_i−2ei​ conditions when odd-coordinate operators are included. Apply Theorem 3.2. ◻

In dimension two the two-diagonal fixed sets are the downward pyramidal sets of the square isoperimetric argument. They differ from ordinary checkerboard corner ideals. In any dimension they give an exact finite recurrence over their fixed family, since both neighborhoods and intersections remain fixed. The theorem does not bound the number of these ideals by a polynomial in ddd or in nnn.

Remark 3.7 (Why even path factors require another idea). Every parity-preserving strategy compression on an even path is the identity. Each endpoint is the unique degree-one vertex in its color. Applying (8) to its singleton forces that singleton to be fixed. Fixed sets are closed under neighborhoods, so every NtN^tNt of either endpoint is fixed. These are the spacing-two prefixes from the two ends. Intersections of suitable prefixes isolate every singleton; fixed intersections follow from monotonicity and cardinality, without idempotence. Thus all singletons, and consequently all sets, are fixed. This rules out a nontrivial even-path factor reduction within this specific comparison framework. It does not rule out richer state labels or different comparison theorems.

An exact two-count game

Corollary 4.4. For every daily budget on every odd-by-odd rectangle, the unrestricted minimum capture time is exactly the shortest-path distance from (E,M)(E,M)(E,M) to (0,0)(0,0)(0,0) in the following two-count state graph: (u,v)⟶(g1(j),g0(i)),0≤i≤u,0≤j≤v,u+v−i−j≤m.(u,v)\longrightarrow (g_1(j),g_0(i)),\qquad 0\leq i\leq u,\quad0\leq j\leq v,\quad u+v-i-j\leq m.(u,v)⟶(g1​(j),g0​(i)),0≤i≤u,0≤j≤v,u+v−i−j≤m. A shortest path gives an optimal physical strategy by deleting suffixes of the two current-color prefix orders. The reduction also respects arbitrary prescribed daily budgets.

Proof. Define C(S)=I0(∣S∩V0∣)∪I1(∣S∩V1∣).C(S)=I_0(|S\cap V_0|)\cup I_1(|S\cap V_1|).C(S)=I0​(∣S∩V0​∣)∪I1​(∣S∩V1​∣). It is monotone, cardinality preserving and idempotent. By the exact profiles and nesting, N(C(S))∩V1−p=I1−p(gp(∣S∩Vp∣))⊆I1−p(∣N(S∩Vp)∣).N(C(S))\cap V_{1-p} =I_{1-p}(g_p(|S\cap V_p|)) \subseteq I_{1-p}(|N(S\cap V_p)|).N(C(S))∩V1−p​=I1−p​(gp​(∣S∩Vp​∣))⊆I1−p​(∣N(S∩Vp​)∣). The last set is the corresponding part of C(N(S))C(N(S))C(N(S)). Apply Theorem 3.2. Every displayed transition is also the exact neighborhood of the indicated survivors, so it has a physical realization. Shortest paths, with infinity for an unreachable zero state, settle both feasibility and minimum time. ◻

The corollary is an exact recurrence for every parameter, rather than a closed expression for its shortest-path distance. It avoids imposing an unproved sequential allocation to the two initial colors: both may receive inspections on any day.

An exact isoperimetric order in every all-odd box

The preceding rectangle theorem extends to every dimension. The extension uses a weighted exchange argument: compression in lower-dimensional faces first makes neighborhood size a sum of local costs, and an order comparison then identifies exchanges that cannot increase that sum. Parity-restricted isoperimetry on hypercubes was studied by Körner and Wei (1984), and local-to-global methods for Cartesian-product vertex boundaries by Bezrukov and Serra (2002). Here the neighborhood is the open neighborhood of a single color class. We give the face compressions and their exchange argument explicitly, rather than infer the result from a theorem about closed vertex boundaries.

Delete any factors of side length one, and write the remaining box as B=∏i=1d{0,…,Li},2≤L1≤⋯≤Ld,Li even.B=\prod_{i=1}^d\{0,\ldots,L_i\},\qquad 2\le L_1\le\cdots\le L_d,\qquad L_i\text{ even}.B=i=1∏d​{0,…,Li​},2≤L1​≤⋯≤Ld​,Li​ even. Thus coordinates are ordered from the shortest side to the longest. Let BpB_pBp​ be its color-ppp class, where the color of xxx is the parity of ∣x∣=∑ixi|x|=\sum_i x_i∣x∣=∑i​xi​. Within either color, order vertices by increasing ∣x∣|x|∣x∣ and then by decreasing lexicographic coordinates. Write x≺yx\prec yx≺y for this order and Ip(k)I_p(k)Ip​(k) for its first kkk vertices. The direction of the lexicographic tie is part of the definition.

Theorem 5.1 (Compatible isoperimetric nesting in all-odd boxes). For every S⊆BpS\subseteq B_pS⊆Bp​, ∣N(S)∣≥∣N(Ip(∣S∣))∣.|N(S)|\ge |N(I_p(|S|))|.∣N(S)∣≥∣N(Ip​(∣S∣))∣. Moreover, N(Ip(k))N(I_p(k))N(Ip​(k)) is a prefix in the opposite color. Consequently the minimum capture time for every inspection budget on BBB is given by an exact recurrence on O(∣B∣2)O(|B|^2)O(∣B∣2) states, and optimal inspection sets can be recovered from that recurrence.

For d=1d=1d=1 the minimizing order is the spacing-two prefix order of Lemma 3.4. For d=2d=2d=2, putting the shorter coordinate first and ordering it decreasingly within a weight layer is equivalent to the increasing-long-coordinate convention of Theorem 4.1. These provide the induction bases. In particular, the higher-dimensional assertion does not assume a general Cartesian-product isoperimetric principle.

Prefix neighborhoods and a local cost identity

Lemma 5.2 (Nesting of prefix neighborhoods). For the stated weight and lexicographic order, the neighborhood of a prefix is a prefix of the opposite color. This statement holds even without the assumptions that the side lengths are odd and sorted.

Proof. Within a fixed weight layer, ℓ\ellℓ preserves order, allowing ties. Indeed, suppose z≺wz\prec wz≺w first differ in coordinate iii, so zi>wiz_i>w_izi​>wi​. Otherwise j(z)=ij(z)=ij(z)=i and zi−1≥wiz_i-1\ge w_izi​−1≥wi​. A strict inequality preserves the order. In the equality case the tail of www has total weight one; removing its unique unit gives ℓ(z)=ℓ(w)\ell(z)=\ell(w)ℓ(z)=ℓ(w).

Consider a nonempty prefix whose last, possibly partial, layer has weight rrr. Every smaller opposite-color layer is completely covered: its nonzero vertices have lower neighbors in complete source layers. When weight zero belongs to the opposite color, it is covered by the first odd layer. No vertex above layer r+1r+1r+1 is covered. On layer r+1r+1r+1, a vertex is covered precisely when its earliest lower neighbor belongs to the selected prefix in layer rrr. The order preservation just proved makes these covered vertices an initial interval of layer r+1r+1r+1. The empty prefix is immediate. ◻

Call a set pair-compressed if, after fixing all but any two coordinates, its selected vertices in either free-coordinate parity form a prefix of the inherited order. Face compression and its partial order

Suppose d≥3d\ge3d≥3 and the isoperimetric theorem has been proved in dimension d−1d-1d−1. On each fixed color define a partial order ≤P\le_P≤P​ as the reflexive transitive closure of x<Pyif x≺y and xi=yi for at least one i. x<_P y\quad\hbox{if }x\prec y \hbox{ and }x_i=y_i\hbox{ for at least one }i. x<P​yif x≺y and xi​=yi​ for at least one i.(23) All generating relations increase the total order, so this is indeed a partial order. Its ideals are exactly the sets whose restriction to every codimension-one fiber is a prefix.

The inductive isoperimetric theorem and compatible neighborhood nesting make the prefix map on each (d−1)(d-1)(d−1)-dimensional box a strategy compression: it is monotone, preserves cardinality, and sends each color’s neighborhood into the corresponding prefix of the original neighborhood’s size. The remaining side lengths are still sorted, and their order is the restriction of the global order to a fixed-coordinate fiber. By Lemma 3.3, compressing all such fibers for one coordinate index is a strategy compression of BBB.

Cycle through the ddd indices. Every change strictly decreases the sum of the selected vertices’ positions in the global weight and lexicographic order. This nonnegative integer is bounded by ∣B∣(∣B∣−1)/2|B|(|B|-1)/2∣B∣(∣B∣−1)/2. The simultaneous-compression argument in Section 3 therefore gives a uniform finite composition whose output is fixed by every face compression. In particular, every S⊆BpS\subseteq B_pS⊆Bp​ can be replaced by a PPP-ideal of the same size without increasing its neighborhood.

Every PPP-ideal is pair-compressed. A two-coordinate fiber lies inside a codimension-one fiber obtained by fixing a coordinate outside the pair; such a coordinate exists because d≥3d\ge3d≥3. The restriction of a prefix to a subfiber is a prefix of its inherited order. Thus Lemma 5.3 applies to the resulting ideals.

Proof of Theorem 5.1. The path and rectangle bases were noted above. In dimension d≥3d\ge3d≥3, the inductive face compressions replace an arbitrary S⊆BpS\subseteq B_pS⊆Bp​ by a PPP-ideal of the same size and with no larger neighborhood. The empty set needs no further argument.

If a nonempty PPP-ideal is not a global prefix, let xxx be its earliest missing vertex and yyy its latest included vertex. Then x≺yx\prec yx≺y. They are incomparable in PPP: x≤Pyx\le_P yx≤P​y would contradict ideality, and y≤Pxy\le_P xy≤P​x would contradict the global order. By Lemma 5.5, a(x)≤a(y)a(x)\le a(y)a(x)≤a(y).

Replace yyy by xxx. Removing yyy preserves ideality because every proper successor of yyy is later in the global order and hence absent. Adding xxx preserves ideality because every proper predecessor of xxx is earlier and hence present; yyy is not such a predecessor. The new set has the same positive cardinality and color. The neighborhood cost identity (22) shows that its neighborhood does not increase. The sum of global positions strictly decreases, so iteration ends at the global prefix of that size. This proves the isoperimetric inequality. Lemma 5.2 gives compatible nesting, completing the induction. ◻

The upper bound also admits a direct description. Spend all m=u0+1m=u_0+1m=u0​+1 inspections on one current prefix cohort. Define C(S)=I0(∣S∩B0∣)∪I1(∣S∩B1∣).C(S)=I_0(|S\cap B_0|)\cup I_1(|S\cap B_1|).C(S)=I0​(∣S∩B0​∣)∪I1​(∣S∩B1​∣). Isoperimetry and nesting imply that CCC is an idempotent strategy compression. Remark 5.7. Every weight and lexicographic prefix is a checkerboard corner ideal: a distinct coordinatewise smaller vertex of the same parity has smaller weight. Hence the theorem also proves a corner-ideal normal form for the full-board game on every all-odd box. It does not assert that a global prefix can replace an arbitrary prescribed partial starting set without altering its optimum, and it does not settle boxes with even side lengths. The all-odd-box result gives exact feasibility, minimum time, and strategies through a polynomial recurrence; a uniform closed arithmetic expression for that time is a further question.

Attaining schedules for every budget

For an actual diagonal prefix, when its survivor size is between two and h−3h-3h−3, movement adds exactly two. A singleton has at most three neighbors, all inspectable next day because m≥3m\ge3m≥3. When r=1r=1r=1, choose the first cohort’s initial reflected orientation so that the singleton survivor on its qqqth full-budget day is a corner. Its next support has two rooms. The extreme budgets are immediate. A perfect matching gives ∣N(B)∣≥∣B∣|N(B)|\ge|B|∣N(B)∣≥∣B∣ for arbitrary mixed-parity room sets. One day requires all 2h=4n2h=4n2h=4n rooms. The two-probe barrier proved above establishes infeasibility for all m≤2m\le2m≤2. Five rows

The first budget beyond the four-row classification admits another uniform formula. The two parities of the long side require different lower arguments.

Theorem 10.1 (Five rows, three inspections). For every n≥5n\ge5n≥5, T3(P5□Pn)=10n−20. T_3(P_5\mathbin{\square}P_n)=10n-20. The matching upper construction has the same insertion property. A serial strategy directs the full budget to one initial cohort until it can be eliminated, uses any unused quota on that finishing day on the other cohort, and then directs the full budget to the other.

Lemma 11.3 (Insertion in a serial strategy). Under (57), suppose a base serial strategy visits count ccc in each active cohort before an inspection. An enlarged rectangle with majority size H+ΔH+\DeltaH+Δ has a strategy taking exactly 4Δ4\Delta4Δ more days.

Proof. Under a full-budget inspection an active cohort’s size never increases, because every neighborhood surplus is at most mmm. The certified visit to ccc is therefore reached from above, and the subsequent base trajectory stays at or below ccc. Above the cut, the enlarged active trajectory is the translation by Δ\DeltaΔ of the base trajectory, by the high profile translation identity in the preceding proof. The uninspected cohort remains its full current color class. When the first active cohort reaches c+Δc+\Deltac+Δ, insert 2Δ2\Delta2Δ full-budget days. Throughout this inserted interval the profile plateaus give g0(k−m)=k−1,g1(k−m)=k.g_0(k-m)=k-1,\qquad g_1(k-m)=k.g0​(k−m)=k−1,g1​(k−m)=k. Every two days reduce its size by one and restore its current color. The inserted block therefore ends at ccc with the phase of the base schedule unchanged. Follow the base trajectory below the cut.

The first cohort’s finishing-day unused quota is unchanged. The second cohort consequently begins its active phase at the translated base state. This state is above the cut: it lies within m+1m+1m+1 of a full color class, whereas (57) places ccc farther from that edge. Follow its translated trajectory until c+Δc+\Deltac+Δ, insert another 2Δ2\Delta2Δ full-budget days, and then finish along the unchanged lower trajectory. Both inserted blocks have even length, so the later phases of the schedule agree with those in the base strategy. ◻

The two insertion proofs also apply to any other compatible profile family with color-class sizes H,H−1H,H-1H,H−1 and a fixed budget mmm, provided that a corner radius AAA has the following properties: every surplus is between −1-1−1 and mmm; the central profiles are k+m−1k+m-1k+m−1 and k+mk+mk+m; the low profiles are unchanged when the remaining tail exceeds AAA; and the high profiles translate when the source count exceeds AAA. These are exactly the properties used in the displacement, collar, and trajectory arguments. In that formulation one sets D=m+1D=m+1D=m+1 and uses the same margin and affine-collar conditions. This observation will also give an exact three-dimensional family below.

After an active cohort loses ddd on an efficient day, its potential is strictly below Γ\GammaΓ. If it is still positive, (72) forces it to stay active on the next efficient day. Call a day clean when all mmm inspections target one cohort and the other cohort is actually empty or actually its full current color class. Flat potential alone is insufficient for this conclusion. We now bound the transient days needed to reach actual emptiness or fullness.

Therefore an uninspected nonempty proper prefix grows by at least one every two days until it is full.

The preceding compression theorems work in arbitrary dimension, but do not by themselves provide a closed time formula for every box. We give two unbounded applications and a fully certified three-dimensional example.

There is a useful further recurrence even when global minimizing prefixes are unavailable. Let a bipartite transverse graph QQQ have compatible minimizing parity orders with profiles g0,g1g_0,g_1g0​,g1​. For a one-color support in Q□PnQ\mathbin{\square}P_nQ□Pn​, let kjk_jkj​ be its size in column j=0,…,n−1j=0,\ldots,n-1j=0,…,n−1, and let ppp be its global color.

Proposition 13.2. For each prescribed column-count vector, the exact minimum neighborhood size is ∑j=0n−1max⁡{g(p+j) mod 2(kj),kj−1,kj+1},k−1=kn=0.\sum_{j=0}^{n-1} \max\{g_{(p+j)\bmod2}(k_j),k_{j-1},k_{j+1}\}, \qquad k_{-1}=k_n=0.j=0∑n−1​max{g(p+j)mod2​(kj​),kj−1​,kj+1​},k−1​=kn​=0. This holds for every positive nnn, including even nnn.

Proof. In column jjj, the neighborhood is the union of the transverse neighborhood of that column and the supports in the two adjacent columns. Its size is at least the displayed maximum. Replace every column support by the corresponding transverse prefix. All three sets are now prefixes of the same opposite color order, and their union has size exactly the maximum. These replacements attain all column minima simultaneously. ◻

Minimize the sum over vectors with ∑kj=k\sum k_j=k∑kj​=k to obtain the exact global cardinality profile. A transfer state remembers the previous count aaa, current count bbb, and cumulative count. Appending ccc charges max⁡{g(b),a,c}\max\{g(b),a,c\}max{g(b),a,c} and replaces the pair by (b,c)(b,c)(b,c). Zero counts at the two outside columns give the boundary conditions. Writing W=∣Q∣W=|Q|W=∣Q∣, this direct recurrence uses O(n2W4)O(n^2W^4)O(n2W4) arithmetic operations and O(nW3)O(nW^3)O(nW3) memory once the transverse profiles are known. It applies in particular to every all-odd cross-section.

This computes exact neighborhood minima, not compatible global orders. The minimizing vector can depend on kkk without being nested. A search using only these cardinality profiles therefore supplies a lower time bound; it is not asserted to attain that bound on arbitrary even cylinders. The accompanying code checks the recurrence against all 524 288524\,288524288 one-color supports of the 3×3×43\times3\times43×3×4 box.

In Lean the corresponding distance potentials are stored as finite integers and checked to be nondecreasing in both counts, zero at zero, and to drop by at most one under every relaxed transition. This proves the lower bound without trusting the search routine that found the potentials. For budgets at most four, there is a shorter proof: every same-color triple has at least seven neighbors, so a cohort of at least seven positions can never fall below seven after four inspections and movement.

Larger budgets inherit these schedules. Fewer than 272727 probes cannot capture every possible initial room in one day, and 272727 can. We have therefore proved the complete table stated in the introduction. Its geometry, finite inequalities, physical schedules, and interpretation as capture of every actual target walk are all checked in Lean.

A uniform height strategy for cylinders

Theorem 13.3. If HHH is any finite bipartite graph with A≥1A\ge1A≥1 vertices and n≥2n\ge2n≥2, then h(H□Pn)≤⌊A/2⌋+1.h(H\mathbin{\square}P_n)\le\left\lfloor A/2\right\rfloor+1.h(H□Pn​)≤⌊A/2⌋+1. For m>A/2m>A/2m>A/2, at most 2⌈A(n+2)/(2m−A)⌉2\left\lceil A(n+2)/(2m-A)\right\rceil2⌈A(n+2)/(2m−A)⌉ days suffice.

Proof. We first clear one initial-color cohort. Write the path coordinate as 0≤z<n0\le z<n0≤z<n. Bound the possible positions in each fiber by a cutoff ava_vav​, of the current required parity, such that ∣au−av∣=1|a_u-a_v|=1∣au​−av​∣=1 whenever uvuvuv is an edge of HHH. Initially take av=n−1a_v=n-1av​=n−1 or n−2n-2n−2 according to its parity; this bounds the full cohort. Cutoffs may later be negative or exceed the board.

At a local maximum vvv, lower ava_vav​ by two. Record the room at the old height if it lies on the board. Every adjacent difference stays one. A sequence of mmm such virtual operations records at most mmm distinct rooms: repeated operations in a fiber use strictly decreasing heights. Inspect those rooms simultaneously. The survivors lie below the new cutoffs av′a'_vav′​. After movement their cutoffs are bounded by av′+1a'_v+1av′​+1: a path move increases height by at most one, and an HHH-move arrives from uuu with au′≤av′+1a'_u\le a'_v+1au′​≤av′​+1.

Choose the virtual operations in a fixed cyclic order. List first the initially higher color class of HHH, then the other class, and repeat this AAA-letter word. Every operation is at a local maximum; after a whole color class has been lowered, the other is higher. Adding one to all cutoffs after a day changes no comparison. Isolated vertices of HHH cause no difficulty.

After ttt days every vertex has been lowered at least ⌊mt/A⌋\left\lfloor mt/A\right\rfloor⌊mt/A⌋ times, so max⁡vav(t)≤n−1+t−2⌊mt/A⌋<n+1−t(2m−A)/A.\max_v a_v(t)\le n-1+t-2\left\lfloor mt/A\right\rfloor < n+1-t(2m-A)/A.vmax​av​(t)≤n−1+t−2⌊mt/A⌋<n+1−t(2m−A)/A. The displayed number of days per cohort makes every cutoff negative. Since H□PnH\mathbin{\square}P_nH□Pn​ has no isolated vertices, an empty post-movement belief certifies capture during inspection. Repeat for the other initial cohort, starting with the full bound of its then-current parity. ◻

Proof. For n≥3n\ge3n≥3 the board contains the three-cube. An evader may choose to stay in that subgraph, so its hunting number is at least five. Theorem 13.3 gives the upper bound with A=9A=9A=9. At n=1n=1n=1 use the rectangle theorem; at n=2n=2n=2 use Theorem 13.1 with the 3×33\times33×3 base. ◻

For a general box this construction can be applied along a longest axis, giving ⌊(∏i≠jni)/2⌋+1\left\lfloor(\prod_{i\ne j}n_i)/2\right\rfloor+1⌊(∏i=j​ni​)/2⌋+1 as a sufficient budget. It can be loose. In particular the complete time classification of longer 3×3×n3\times3\times n3×3×n cylinders remains open here.

Formal verification, reproducibility, and open problems

The formal development uses Lean 4.33.1 and its standard library. It contains no admitted proof, project-specific mathematical axiom, or trusted external solver result. Finite certificates are reduced by the Lean kernel. The dependency reports of the final theorems use only the usual logical principles of propositional extensionality, classical choice, and quotient soundness, where applicable.

Three graph classifications are complete in Lean:

  • PathClassification.can_capture_iff and exact_minimum cover every positive path length and budget, including the one-room and one-probe cases.

  • LadderGame connects the complete two-counter optimum to actual two-row rooms, daily cardinality budgets, and arbitrary avoiding walks, including the single-edge degeneration.

  • ThreeCubeTimeClassification.can_capture_iff and exact_minimum cover every budget on the 3×3×33\times3\times33×3×3 box. The statement quantifies over unrestricted room-valued inspection schedules. It does not assume a preferred order or support shape.

The abstract strategy-comparison theorem is also formalized in StrategyCompression. Its concrete odd-path and square operators currently have ordinary proofs. The three-row and four-row classifications, five-row classifications, arbitrary-dimensional odd-box isoperimetry, general side-two application, and unbounded cylinder construction also currently have ordinary proofs, not complete Lean developments. The scalar potentials in the five-row proofs have separate Lean checks, including row-deficit consequences, the four-probe transition and equality lemmas, and the three finite high-budget bounds. The discounted potential for five or more probes and the entire physical-geometric bridge are not yet formalized. Successful checking of the formal files must not be represented as formal verification of those additional theorems.

The generic profile complement identity and the one-unit difference of the maximum neighborhood surpluses for bipartite parts of sizes M+1,MM+1,MM+1,M are fully formalized. The module is BipartiteProfileDuality; its inverse arithmetic is in ProfileInverse. The profiles are defined as actual attained neighborhood minima over finite subsets; they are not assumed functions. This verifies the structural profile identity used in the odd-box feasibility corollary, while its geometric nesting and the published hunting-number criterion remain ordinary mathematical dependencies. The minimum-budget interval-insertion theorem and its rational certificates also currently have ordinary proofs and independent exact checks, rather than Lean proofs. The uniform minimum-budget scalar inequality is verified in UniformOddRank; the eventual-period theorem for odd cylinders and its geometric corner decomposition currently have ordinary proofs.

The possible-position semantics are proved in BeliefSemantics: membership is equivalent to the existence of a legal walk avoiding earlier probes. The finite winning recurrence and its greatest losing trap are proved in CaptureRecurrence. Formal rounds start at zero, so a last-round index ttt corresponds to t+1t+1t+1 inspection days. Every public classification has been separately reviewed for this indexing, its physical graph, its global daily budget, and its quantification over all walks.

The companion at https://angelraychev.com/princess/ provides the presentation, detailed proof text, and formal sources. The research archive includes scripts for independent physical replay, finite lower certificates, exact small-instance searches, and a dated research log. The source-specific verification receipt records the compiler version, source hashes, dependency order, axiom reports, and exit codes. The complete check runs sequentially with one compiler worker. To reproduce it, install the pinned Lean version and run python3 src/check_lean.py from the archive root, optionally giving --lean followed by the compiler path. No additional package installation is required.

What remains open in this investigation

The main unresolved target is a comparably concise account of feasibility and minimum time for arbitrary side lengths in arbitrary dimension. The exact algorithms proved here cover substantial unbounded families; they are not a closed classification of every box. Even where an exact recurrence is established, solving it in a useful explicit form remains a distinct problem. Numerical patterns are recorded as conjectures until the required geometry and all parameter ranges are proved.

The arbitrary-dimensional odd-box theorem is established by a uniform exchange argument, extending the two-dimensional base without inferring an unbounded statement from numerical checks. Boxes with even sides greater than two require further ideas: parity-open nesting already fails on some even rectangles. Also, optimal strategies often finish one initial-color cohort before working substantially on the other, with one shared transition day; an unrestricted exchange theorem that would justify this pattern in every case is not presently asserted.

Research and writing provenance

The path results originated in the author’s October 2019–March 2020 work. The present shorter proofs were reconstructed from the historical manuscripts; the original work’s credit is not reassigned to the tool used for reconstruction. The 2026 grid and box investigation, new proof organizations, experiments, formal developments, and this draft were developed with substantial assistance from Astra 6 operating through the Codex harness. The research log distinguishes recovered results, known literature, new derivations with unverified priority, failed approaches, and unresolved claims. The human author retains responsibility for the manuscript and any eventual submission.
